correctness.rationale: The pencils of lines through one center and of conics through four centers give the stated four decompositions into exceptional curves, over an algebraic closure in any characteristic. Testing intersection zero with each pencil in the marked Picard lattice independently reconstructs the support matrix. The odd five-bit words record which support in each complementary pencil pair contains each line. Invariants are generated by actual orbit sums, so the matrix counts pencils in a source orbit against a single fixed line, without division by orbit lengths. The independent calculation matches every orbit count, rank and torsion factor in the eighteen rows. An additional structural check is to view the rational image as affine functions on the odd cube. An integer-valued affine function has integral coefficients or all coefficients half-integral, by comparing singleton words and words differing by two added coordinates. Fixed functions have one free linear coefficient per positive signed cycle and none per negative cycle, plus constants. Normalizing the signs along each cycle, the invariant incidence image is generated by the positive-cycle coordinate sums and by constant functions equal to the lengths of the cycles. A negative cycle precludes the half-integral coset; if all cycles are positive that coset has index two over the integral-coefficient functions. The resulting torsion indices are 1 for a negative cycle, 2 for all-positive types other than the five-cycle, and 10 for the five-cycle. The displayed five-cycle minors independently show cyclic torsion. The proof's parenthetical at line 52 is an editorial artifact: rank six means precisely four zero positions among the ten Smith positions, as the following text correctly says.
residual_risks: The classification is conditional on the actual Weyl type; it does not assert that all types occur over each field.

Same-degree integral trace and five-cycle torus comparisons
value.rationale: Integral generation by rational orbit combinations of conic supports is a natural descent question on two canonical geometric label schemes. The complete outcome distinguishes geometric Smith torsion from arithmetic orbit-sum torsion and identifies exactly when a new prime appears. The small positive five-cycle witness is a meaningful boundary of what geometry alone predicts, rather than an arbitrary field sample.
residual_risks: No cohomological or Brauer interpretation of the resulting formal torsion is demonstrated.
